Transcript:
[00:00] Eli: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 40 minutes, um quick intros — elI from redwood, sofia on the infra side, and then priya, mark, ana from thermion?
[00:10] Priya: yep that's us, thanks.
[00:12] Sofia: hi all, we'll jump into the numbers then the tuning suggestions, cool?
[00:18] Mark: sounds good, let's try to be concrete, we only have a short runway to decide about dedicated nodes.
[00:24] Eli: yeah, got it. quick recap: last week we ran the 50k request pilot across the two conversation routes, we measured tokens per dollar and tokens per second, also KV cache hit rate when prefix enabled.
[00:36] Priya: curious, what's the headline tps/$, because our CFO keeps asking tokens per dollar not just latency.
[00:42] Eli: headline — on the hosted small-rho profile we saw about 0.9k tokens per dollar for the base model, with quantized variant up to 1.6k tokens per dollar. that's averaged across mixed prompt lengths, so it's noisy.
[00:56] Ana: can you unpack 'small-rho profile' — i think our engineers misheard that as 'small GPU'?
[01:02] Sofia: yeah sorry that's our shorthand for the mid-range instance class (the g-optim-48k-ish), name escapes me in the transcript, but it's the profile we matched to your latency SLO (150ms median).
[01:14] Priya: ok, numbers look promising. what about tokens/sec? if we burst, does the unit econ change?
[01:20] Eli: yes — tokens/sec improved with batching; single-request mode gave 200 tokens/sec per GPU on average, batching up to 8 improved aggregate to 1.4k tokens/sec but per-request p99 jumped ~30-40ms when batch windows exceeded 40ms. so it's a tradeoff.
[01:36] Mark: that p99 increase is a problem for some of our latency-sensitive flows, we can't push batch windows too high. any middle ground?
[01:42] Sofia: two levers — adaptive batching (we recommend the autoscaler profile we sent) and partial batching only for background/async routes. for sync routes keep batch size 1-2, for async set 4-8. also the KV cache reduces token counts when the user history repeats.
[01:58] Priya: our dataset has a lot of repeated prefixes — about 30% of sessions reuse the same question stems. how effective was caching?
[02:06] Eli: across the run we saw KV/prefix cache hit rates ~22% end-to-end, which translated into 18-26% token savings depending on prompt length. longer contexts saw higher relative savings. the caveat: cache warmup and eviction policy matters.
[02:20] Ana: what's the eviction policy rn? we saw the default TTL was too short in our first run.
[02:24] Sofia: default LRU with 10k entries, TTL 1 hour in the hosted pilot. For your workload we suggested bumping TTL to 4 hours and pinning hot keys for the top 200 prefixes, that improved steady-state hit rate in our staging tests.
[02:38] Mark: ok but pinning means memory cost on the infer nodes right? can you estimate the RAM delta?
[02:43] Sofia: ballpark — each cached KV pair is ~1.2MB for your average sequence, 200 pinned keys ~240MB per node. it's not huge relative to a 96GB GPU node, but yes it's non-zero.
[02:55] Priya: interesting. what about quantization impact on quality? we worry about hallucinations creeping up.
[03:00] Eli: good question — in the eval set we saw a minor BLEU/ROUGE-ish delta, the quantized 4-bit variant increased a few low-confidence hallucinations on rare tokens, but for your primary NLU intents the fidelity remained >98%. we logged the failures in the eval report. i'll attach.
[03:18] Priya: please do. CFO-wise, the switch to quantized gave us near 80% cost reduction per token in the heavy tails in your numbers, correct?
[03:26] Eli: roughly, for long outputs the per-token compute is lower, so you see up to 50-60% cost improvement versus baseline, depending on sequence length. overall tokens/$ went from 0.9k to 1.6k as i said.
[03:38] Ana: any concerns about SSO or audit logs for a dedicated deployment? security caught some minor stuff last run.
[03:44] Sofia: for dedicated we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. also KMS for keys at rest. we flagged an item about trace retention with your security team last week — do you want the details in this thread?
[03:59] Mark: yes please, send the specifics. retention windows are a big ask for compliance.
[04:04] Eli: will do.
[04:06] Priya: circling back to the economics: you mentioned autoscaler suggestion — what parameters should we tune first?
[04:11] Sofia: the two highest-impact knobs are batch window (ms) and target tokens per batch. start conservative: batch window 20ms for sync flows, target batch size 3. For background workers batch window 60ms, target 6. Also set the cache warmup target 30% in the initial ramp to avoid thrash.
[04:28] Priya: okay, can we get that as a ready-to-apply config? we want infra to push it to staging tomorrow.
[04:33] Eli: yes — action item for Sofia to produce a YAML we can apply.
[04:38] Ana: performance question — can we simulate dedicated node contention vs hosted fallback? in case of spike we need graceful degradation.
[04:45] Sofia: yes we have routing policies — region fallback and model-fallback to a cheaper quantized variant. that will change unit econ but keep service up. we can run a chaos benchmark to show how much tokens/$ changes during failover, typically you see a 20-40% cost delta but latency stays within a higher SLO.
[05:02] Mark: competitor question — we briefly tested Replicate and had lower latency but much higher cost at scale; is that consistent?
[05:08] Eli: Replicate tends to have simpler pricing but less batching and cache optimizations so tokens/$ often worse at production throughput. Anthropic has strong models but their throughput profiles are different. KServe we're seeing in-house teams use for self-hosting when they don't want a managed control plane.
[05:23] Priya: ok. next steps from your side?
[05:26] Eli: i'll send the spreadsheet with per-route token counts, hit-rate breakdown, and suggested batch configs. also include a short note on the quantized quality tradeoffs and the pinned-key memory estimate.
[05:36] Priya: and we'll run the prefix-caching sample and enable the traces. Ana will own that.
[05:40] Ana: yep i'll enable traces and open the access.
[05:42] Sofia: one more note — we recommend a short dedicated benchmark: 30 minute run at 2x expected peak to validate autoscaler thresholds. can we schedule that for next week?
[05:53] Mark: we can do either Thursday or Friday, but need an exact slot.
[05:56] Eli: i'll propose two slots in the calendar right after this call.
[06:00] Priya: great, thanks.

- Recommended config: sync routes: batch window 20ms, target batch 3; async: window 60ms, target 6; TTL bump to 4h, pin top 200 prefixes.
- Security: Redwood supports SAML/RBAC/audit logs; Redwood to send detailed retention and trace handling docs.
